newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Konka sales up 44 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China's Konka sales up 44 pct in 1996.

text.p: Sales at colour television maker Shenzhen Konka Electronic Group Co Ltd rose 44 percent to 5.3 billion yuan in 1996 compared with 3.6 billion yuan in 1995, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said on Friday.
Konka turned out 2.5 million television sets last year against 1.77 million in 1995, the newspaper said, adding that Konka's 1996 overseas sales were US$40 million.
The firm's home sales in 1996 soared more than 90 percent year-on-year due to its successes in a price war among major domestic television producers, the newspaper said.
In early June 1996, Konka reduced its prices by an average of 10 percent to match price cuts by its main competitor, Sichuan Changhong Electric Appliance Co Ltd.
The newspaper said Konka managed to double its domestic market share to 18 percent by the end of the year.

It said this was helped with the purchase last year of two subsidiaries, in Shaanxi and Heilongjiang, which produced 400,000 and 600,000 TV sets respectively and notched up a combined profit of more than 10 million yuan.
It said Konka aimed to make about four million TV sets in 1997 to further expand its market share.
Earlier this month, a company spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that Konka was likely to report a marginal rise in 1996 net profits on stronger sales.
"Konka saw stronger operations in the second half of 1996 as sales picked up after the cuts in its television prices," the official said but declined to give figures.
Konka reported after-tax profits of 265.06 million yuan for 1995, up 17 percent from 226.71 million yuan the previous year, under Chinese accounting standards.
Its unaudited interim net for 1996 edged up 1.7 percent year-on-year to 142.67 million yuan, with sales jumping 21 percent to 2.03 billion yuan.
Konka said its moves to expand market share by lowering the price of most TV models had boosted sales but squeezed margins.
It said in the interim report that it had 11.8 percent of mainland China's market at the end of June last year.
The company said it turned out 970,000 colour TV sets in the first half of this year, up 19.68 percent from the year-earlier period.
